newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower in a consolidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower in a consolidation.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended sharply lower on Thursday, battered by a round of profit taking following December's rise to two-month highs Wednesday, traders said.
"It had a nice run-up and it was due for a mild consolidation," said Merrill Lynch senior analyst Bill O'Neill. "But overall the uptrend is in place."

Traders noted local and commission house selling, as well as options-related selling. They said operators were trying to fill a gap formed early this week between 115.10 and 113.30 cents a lb basis December.
But steady industrial buying held the spot December contract above support at the 116.50 level, with December reaching a low of 116.75 cents.

December ended down 1.85 cents, at 117.45. It rose to an intraday high of 120.50 just after the open. Second-month March finished 1.45 cents lower at 103.65, while the rest closed 0.50 to 2.90 weaker.
The widely watched December/March switch narrowed to 13.80 cents compared to 14.20 cents Wednesday.
Traders said a reporting error announced late Wednesday in certified coffee stocks by the CSCE may have weighed on market sentiment.

The CSCE said the sharp, 24,391-bag drawdown for the week ended October 18 and reported on Monday was due to "past errors in reporting" by one warehouse, but the total 5,583-bag inventory level reported was correct.
"Looking at the drawdown does not change the final results," O'Neill said. "But psychologically it seemed like an excuse for the market to sell off."

Low coffee inventories, combined with delays in the Central American and Mexican coffee harvest due to heavy rains, and mounting worries about truckers' strike in Colombia, should keep prices underpinned, he added.
Volume reached an estimated 6,900 lots, down sharply from Wednesday's official tally of 11,770 lots.
